mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about liquid water is correct?

options.A: Liquid water always has a fixed shape.
options.B: Liquid water always boils at 100°C regardless of the surrounding pressure.
options.C: Liquid water takes the shape of its container but has a definite volume.
options.D: Liquid water is invisible to the naked eye.

mcqs.answer: Liquid water takes the shape of its container but has a definite volume.
mcqs.explanation: Liquid water flows and therefore conforms to the shape of the container it is in, but the amount of water does not change, so it has a definite volume. Option A is false because liquids do not have a fixed shape. Option B is false because the boiling point changes with pressure. Option D is false because liquid water is visible.

mcqs.question: Why can water vapour be present in the air even when the temperature is below 100°C?

options.A: Water vapour is produced only when water reaches its boiling point.
options.B: Some water molecules at the surface have enough kinetic energy to escape into the air at any temperature.
options.C: High air pressure forces water to become vapour only at high altitudes.
options.D: Water vapour is a solid that sublimates directly into gas.

mcqs.answer: Some water molecules at the surface have enough kinetic energy to escape into the air at any temperature.
mcqs.explanation: Even below the boiling point, a few water molecules move fast enough to leave the liquid surface; this process is called evaporation, producing water vapour. Option A confuses evaporation with boiling. Option C misstates the role of pressure. Option D incorrectly describes water vapour as a solid.

mcqs.learning_point: Observable properties of the three states
mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly matches each state of water with its observable property?

options.A: Solid – definite shape and volume; Liquid – takes the shape of its container, definite volume; Gas – definite shape and volume.
options.B: Solid – definite shape, no definite volume; Liquid – no definite shape, definite volume; Gas – no definite shape, no definite volume.
options.C: Solid – definite shape and volume; Liquid – no definite shape but definite volume; Gas – no definite shape and no definite volume.
options.D: Solid – no definite shape, definite volume; Liquid – definite shape, no definite volume; Gas – definite shape, definite volume.

mcqs.answer: Solid – definite shape and volume; Liquid – no definite shape but definite volume; Gas – no definite shape and no definite volume.
mcqs.explanation: A solid keeps both shape and volume, a liquid flows to take the shape of its container while keeping volume, and a gas expands to fill any container, having neither fixed shape nor volume. Options A, B, and D contain incorrect combinations of these properties.

mcqs.learning_point: Water changing from one state to another
mcqs.question: When water changes from one state to another, which process requires the absorption of heat energy from the surroundings?

options.B: Condensation of steam to liquid water
options.D: Deposition of water vapour to ice

mcqs.explanation: Melting (solid to liquid) is an endothermic process; heat must be absorbed from the surroundings to break the ordered structure of ice. Freezing and condensation release heat (exothermic), while deposition (gas to solid) also releases heat.
